title: OpenConnect for Mac
description: OpenConnect client for macOS. Native menu bar UI, WebKit SSO, per-profile routes, split DNS and a command-line interface.
lead: An AnyConnect-compatible VPN client for macOS. OpenConnect handles the tunnel; a native menu bar app and the ocmac CLI manage profiles, sign-in, routes and DNS.
install_description: Install OpenConnect for Mac, import or create a profile, configure routes and DNS, and make a first connection.
requirements: Requires macOS 14.4+, Homebrew and access to an AnyConnect-compatible gateway. The project does not provide VPN servers.
install_note: Run as your regular user. The installer downloads source from GitHub, builds the app and requests administrator access for the system helper. Building may take several minutes.
config_note: One .ocmac file describes one connection. The example sends only 10.0.0.0/8 through the tunnel. DNS for corp.example.com and its subdomains uses the gateway resolver; other domains use the normal connection.
config_auth: This example uses manual password and code entry. Passwords and TOTP secrets can instead come from macOS Keychain, KeePassXC or a command. They are not stored as profile values.
route_text: Only the networks listed in the profile use the tunnel. Routes can be enabled and disabled from the menu.
dns_text: Split DNS uses /etc/resolver entries for listed domains. A gateway search suffix is not the list of domains to resolve through VPN.
sso_text: Cisco single-sign-on-v2 uses a WebKit window. Form rules can be recorded during sign-in. Expired authentication may require user input.
pause_text: Removes the app’s routes and DNS settings while retaining the tunnel session. Resume restores them.
recovery_text: The supervisor monitors the selected connection. Use autoconnect resume to restore it after an outage. Disconnect clears the selected connection.
csd_text: Device assessment depends on the gateway. Use an organization-approved wrapper. A script can be embedded in a profile; opening a file does not execute it.
limits_text: Used on macOS 26, Apple Silicon, with an AnyConnect-compatible gateway and Keycloak. Automated tests cover ocserv and synthetic SSO forms. They do not verify a production Okta or Microsoft Entra ID deployment.
limits_more: Minimum deployment target: macOS 14.4. Intel and macOS 14.4–15 have not been verified on real devices. A clean installation and first sign-in on another Mac have not been verified. IPv6 tunnel routes are not configured.
disclaimer: Independent project. Not affiliated with Cisco or the OpenConnect project.
